title: Principal Security Engineer (AppSec)
description:
Hello. We’re Teya.

Teya was founded on a simple belief: local businesses deserve better.

They are the cafés, restaurants, salons, shops and entrepreneurs that bring character to our high streets, create jobs and keep communities moving. Yet for too long, financial services has made life harder for them - with clunky tools, poor support and complexity that gets in the way of running a business.

Teya exists to change that.

We’re building a financial platform for local businesses across Europe - one built around simple tools, thoughtful design and real human support. Our Members rely on us to help them run their business with confidence, and that responsibility shapes the way we work.

We move fast. We care about quality. We stay close to the detail. And we believe great performance and genuine hospitality should go hand in hand.

If you want to build meaningful products, solve real problems and make a genuine difference for local businesses, we’d love to hear from you

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're a regulated payments fintech operating across multiple European markets, scaling into banking-licence territory. Security Engineering is being rebuilt around a joint operating model with our product, platform, and infrastructure teams. We're hiring a Principal Security Engineer to own the application security side of that model: how software gets designed, built, reviewed, and shipped safely across a growing engineering estate, and how security shows up as an accelerator rather than a toll gate.

This is not a review-queue role, and it is not a role about counting findings. We're not looking for someone to triage scanner output, chase "critical" CVE counts, or sign off tickets. We want an engineer who changes how the company builds software: transforming our SDLC into a secure SDLC, placing controls where they deliver the most value for the least friction, and making the secure path the default path.

The thread running through everything here is influence. You will spend as much time with engineers, product managers, designers, operations, and compliance colleagues as you do with code and tooling. The person who succeeds in this role is the person who can walk into any team, explain the risk in language that team actually uses, and leave them better equipped than when they arrived.

WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

FIRST 90 DAYS

- Understand how we actually build. Map our real delivery paths, from idea to production, across the teams that matter most. Find where security currently lands too late, too heavily, or not at all.

- Baseline the application estate. Establish a clear, honest view of coverage, risk, and the gaps between them. We would rather know the truth early than have a tidy dashboard.

- Start building relationships. Embed with engineering teams, run threat modelling with them rather than for them, and use those sessions to demonstrate what good looks like in practice.

- Identify high-leverage controls. Identify what changes to the SDLC would measurably reduce risk while making delivery faster.

FIRST YEAR

- Secure SDLC transformation. Design and roll out the controls, patterns, and checkpoints that make up our SSDLC. Proportionate, evidence-based, and justified by impact, not by convention.

- Shift-left in practice, not as a slogan. Secure defaults in templates, libraries, and paved roads so that the easiest way to build something is also the safe way. Developers should hit guardrails rarely, and understand them when they do.

- Pipeline-embedded controls. Work with the platform team to extend policy-as-code and build upon existing pipeline security toolchain (SAST, SCA, secrets, or DAST for example). Checks that run in the pipeline and produce signal engineers trust, not noise they learn to ignore.

- Threat modelling as routine practice. Make design-stage security a normal part of how teams work, scaled through enablement and templates rather than through your calendar.

Product and application security

title: Staff Developer Relations Engineer
description:
At Render, we’re building the modern cloud platform for developers creating AI-native, full-stack, multi-service applications. Our mission is to eliminate the tradeoff between the power of hyperscalers and the simplicity of developer-friendly platforms-so teams can ship fast, scale reliably, and focus on their product, not infrastructure.

Unlike complex hyperscalers or ephemeral edge/serverless solutions, Render offers a developer-first experience with persistent compute, dynamic autoscaling, built-in orchestration, and observability, allowing teams to launch, scale, and manage real-world applications without writing infrastructure code or managing servers. Whether you're building LLM-powered applications, scalable SaaS products, or async processing pipelines, Render empowers teams to move fast and scale confidently from MVP to millions of users.

Our platform is trusted by over 7 million developers worldwide and continues to grow rapidly. In February 2026, we raised an additional $100M in Series C financing, bringing our total funding to $260M, to accelerate our vision of making cloud infrastructure both powerful and intuitive-designed for the speed of modern AI development.

We’re a diverse and talented team that values craft, velocity, and user experience. If you’re excited to help shape the future of the intelligent cloud and empower developers everywhere, we’d love to hear from you.

APPLYING TO RENDER

We're seeking candidates who possess high integrity, humility, and an insatiable drive to learn. Through reasoned discussions and continuous feedback, we strive to improve both individually and collectively. We foster an environment of mutual trust and respect, empowering effective debate to achieve the best outcomes for our customers and team.

We especially encourage members of underrepresented groups in the tech community to apply and understand that not all successful candidates will meet each requirement listed.

Our interview process is unique to each role, and we value the candidate experience just as much as our customer experience. We hope your conversations with us reflect a thoughtful process that is illuminative, enjoyable, and respectful of your time.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Render is looking for a Staff Developer Relations Engineer to grow usage and word of mouth for Render among developers building full-stack and AI applications. You'll be Render's technical face on stage, in workshops, at meetups, and in the developer and AI ecosystems where our users build.

DX at Render has two halves. DX Engineering builds and maintains Render's tutorials, sample apps, templates, and video library. DevRel takes Render to developers in person and through the communities and partners they trust, then brings what it hears back into the product. You'll set the technical bar and direction for DevRel, and you'll be the person developers and partners go to for a deep, candid answer about running AI workloads on Render.

You'll build the demos and workshop material behind your own talks. When something you build deserves a long life, DX Engineering turns it into a maintained example or template.

This is a remote role within the US, with the option to work out of our headquarters in San Francisco. Expect regular travel for conferences and events.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Represent Render at conferences, meetups, hackathons, podcasts, and livestreams, with talks and live demos on building and running AI agents and full-stack apps.

- Design and run hands-on workshops and hackathons, from the curriculum to the technical setup behind them.

- Set DevRel's technical direction: pick the communities, ecosystems, and events worth investing in, and define what good looks like for talks, workshops, and demos.

- Be the technical counterpart for ecosystem partners such as AI frameworks, agent tooling, and open source projects: joint workshops, co-hosted events, and the integrations worth building together.

- Go deep in technical communities on GitHu
